records.text: Benjamin Netanyahu and Mitt Romney have been close friends since they worked together at Boston Consulting Group in 1976.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: You can't think of Utah without thinking of the Romney family. They are effectively Mormon royalty. And Mitt Romney, as it turns out, is best friends with Bibi (Benjamin Netanyahu). They have a bromance. It's been ... documented for years in the press for over 50 years, longer than I have been alive. These two have been besties. ... We reminded you that they met at the Boston Consulting Group where they both worked and they haven't stopped working together and supporting each other since.
a friendship which began, like I told you, back in 1976 when they were both working for the Boston Consulting Group.

verification.notes: Romney and Netanyahu did overlap at Boston Consulting Group in 1976 and later developed a warm, longstanding friendship. Contemporary accounts also quote Netanyahu saying they did not know each other well at BCG. Thus the shared 1976 origin is supported, but close friends since 1976 overstates what the evidence establishes.

sources.title: On Israel, Romney sees opening against Obama
sources.relevance: Confirms the 1976 BCG overlap and later friendship while quoting Netanyahu that they did not know each other well then.

sources.title: Romney and Netanyahu relationship traces to Boston Consulting Group
sources.relevance: Documents their BCG overlap and longstanding warm relationship.

records.text: After serving in the Navy and Army Special Forces, Bradley D. Hansell worked at Boston Consulting Group, served on Donald Trump's National Security Council, returned to BCG, and was later selected as undersecretary.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: After serving in the military, first in the Navy and then the Army Special Forces Airborne Division, Brad Hansell immediately went to work at ... the Boston Consulting Group. Interesting. After some years, he was then picked to work under Trump (Donald Trump)'s first administration as a member of the National Security Council, and he was to work as the special assistant to President Donald J. Trump for National Security Affairs. When Trump (Donald Trump)'s first term concluded, he went back to the Boston Consulting Group. ... As a principal of the firm for years, he then did a one-off year before being selected again by Trump (Donald Trump), the new term as the undersecretary, which we just told you about.

verification.notes: The official Defense Department biography confirms Hansell’s U.S. Navy service, advisory work with the Iraqi Army Special Operations Forces, employment at Boston Consulting Group, NSC role in the first Trump administration, return to BCG, and later appointment as Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security.

sources.title: Bradley D. Hansell Official Biography
sources.relevance: Primary Defense Department biography confirms the asserted career sequence.

records.text: Financial Times reporting, as summarized by an unnamed website read by Candace Owens, said Project Aurora began in late 2024 as a pro bono feasibility study for the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation and developed over seven months into consulting contracts reportedly worth $4 million.
records.speaker: Financial Times

appearances.snippet: This website tells us—and I'm going to read this website directly—it says, launched in late 2024, Project Aurora was originally framed as a pro bono feasibility study for the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, a Geneva-registered NGO created with backing from U.S. and Israeli security-linked interests. Over seven months, the project evolved into fully billed ... consulting contracts reportedly worth $4 million. According to a series of leaked documents obtained by the Financial Times, the core of the work focused on estimating the financial costs of various scenarios for Gaza’s post-conflict future.

verification.notes: Financial Times reporting describes seven months of Project Aurora work, beginning as a pro bono feasibility study in October 2024 and developing into contracts worth more than $4 million. BCG’s parliamentary response confirms the pro bono start and later for-fee engagement, while stating that BCG ultimately collected no fees.

sources.title: BCG modelled plan to relocate Palestinians from Gaza
sources.relevance: Financial Times reporting confirms the October 2024 pro bono start, seven-month development, and contracts worth more than $4 million.

sources.title: Boston Consulting Group response to the Business and Trade Committee
sources.relevance: BCG’s formal account confirms the pro bono phase and later for-fee engagement, while clarifying that fees were not collected.

conveyance.original_source: Financial Times reporting via an unnamed website summary

records.text: Financial Times reporting, as summarized by an unnamed website read by Candace Owens, said BCG leadership directed Project Aurora to stop in April 2025, two senior partners continued it through May, and BCG dismissed the partners and launched an external audit in July.
records.speaker: Financial Times

appearances.snippet: It tells us that by April of 2025, BCG's senior leadership claimed that they had issued some internal guidance to halt the project because concerns began to mount internally about the nature of the client, that being Israel, the implications of the work and the potential reputational damage. ... But the firm would then say that two senior partners continued the project in defiance of their directives, maintaining an unofficial team and billing through alternative structures. ... The project continued through May of 2025 when the Financial Times story broke. In July, BCG quickly dismissed the two partners and launched an external audit.

verification.notes: BCG’s formal response and contemporaneous reporting say the work continued until late May 2025 and that the responsible partners exited within days after an investigation began then. They do not support an April stop followed by a July dismissal and audit; the stated chronology is materially wrong.

sources.title: Boston Consulting Group response to the Business and Trade Committee
sources.relevance: BCG’s formal chronology says work stopped in late May and the partners exited within days.

sources.title: BCG modelled plan to relocate Palestinians from Gaza
sources.relevance: Contemporaneous reporting corroborates the late-May investigation and dismissal timeline.

records.text: Boston Consulting Group helped develop the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation's logistics and organizational structure and set pricing for private security contractors operating its Gaza food-distribution hubs.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Was also, as we just told you, instrumental in setting up that Gaza Humanitarian Foundation. That's ringing a bell for you. ... The consulting firm helped to develop the logistics, the organizational structure, and they also set the pricing for paying and equipping private security contractors to operate the food distribution hubs in Gaza.

verification.notes: BCG’s formal response confirms organizational, operational, and logistics advice for the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation. Washington Post reporting says BCG designed and ran business operations and set prices for paying and equipping private security contractors at four distribution hubs.

sources.relevance: Reports that BCG designed and ran business operations and set contractor prices at four hubs.

sources.title: Boston Consulting Group response to the Business and Trade Committee
sources.relevance: BCG confirms its operational, organizational, and logistics advice.

records.text: The Times of Israel reported that Johnnie Moore was appointed executive chairman of the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation after CEO Jake Wood quit and Boston Consulting Group abandoned the project.
records.speaker: The Times of Israel

appearances.snippet: Check out this headline, Times of Israel. Gaza Humanitarian Foundation taps U.S. evangelical leader Johnny Moore as the new chairman. ... It tells us that he was appointed as the new executive chairman of the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation, which is the U.S. and Israel-backed organization providing aid to Gazans. ... Its previous CEO, Jake Wood, quit last week and the Boston Consulting Group abandoned the project today.

verification.notes: The Times of Israel reported that GHF appointed Johnnie Moore executive chairman after Jake Wood resigned, and described the change as following Boston Consulting Group’s withdrawal from the project.

sources.title: Gaza Humanitarian Foundation taps Johnnie Moore as new chairman
sources.relevance: Directly confirms Moore’s appointment after Wood’s resignation and BCG’s withdrawal.

records.text: Orbis Operations engaged Boston Consulting Group for a Gaza aid feasibility study on behalf of Israel's Tachlith Institute, and BCG was chosen because of its longstanding relationship with former CIA operative Phil Reilly.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They were initially engaged by Orbis, which is a Washington area security contractor to help with a feasibility study for a new aid project. ... Orbis was prepping the study on behalf of the Tachlith Institute, which is an Israeli think tank. And yeah, BCG was chosen as that consultant because of their longstanding relationship with Phil Reilly, an ex-CIA operative who worked for Orbis—now ex-CIA.

verification.notes: Financial Times reporting says Orbis engaged BCG for work with Israeli group Tachlith and that BCG was selected in part because Orbis founder Philip Reilly had been a BCG consultant. BCG’s formal response independently confirms Orbis was the client.
